candidates.title: uv/poetry runner value-options defeat the hook: `uv run --with/-p/--python/--project/--directory <v> envh ...` returns NO ASK
repro_cmds: echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "uv run --with rich envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py

echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "uv run --python 3.12 envh session start weekly --minutes 5 --reason r"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "uv run -p 3.13 envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py

echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "uv run --project /tmp envh preset propose draft.yaml --reason r"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
candidates.observed_output: ALL FIVE print nothing (NO ASK). Controls that DO ask: `uv run envh run --reason r -- echo hi` -> {"hookSpecificOutput":{..."permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"envh: running one command..."}}; and the equals-form `uv run --with=rich envh run ...` -> ASK. So only the space-separated value form bypasses.
candidates.why_novel: The hook docstring AND README explicitly advertise `uv run` as a handled wrapper ('behind timeout, nohup, env or uv run'). But uv/poetry are in RUNNERS, not WRAPPERS, so command_words() uses WRAPPERS.get('uv', set()) == empty set for their value-options. A space-separated uv option that takes a value (--with, --python/-p, --project, --directory, --index-url, --with-requirements, ...) is therefore treated as a no-value flag (index += 1), and the option's VALUE (e.g. 'rich', '3.12', '/tmp') is taken as the command name. basename('rich') != 'envh', so no envh invocation is detected and passphrase_reason() is never called. This is NOT one of the README's acknowledged bypasses (script file / interpreter one-liner / pipe-into-shell / variable-built).
candidates.notes: Really starts a request: uv run parses the value option, then execs `envh run ...` / `envh session start ...` / etc. These envh invocations have no --session and uv does not set ENVH_SESSION, so op=run arrives with session=None (control.py op_run line 203 `if session_id:` false -> request_run -> console passphrase prompt), and session start / preset propose / non-dry-run import always prompt. uv 0.8.17 is installed at /root/.local/bin/uv and `uv run --help` confirms --with/-w, --python/-p, --project, --directory, --index-url/-i all take a value. Root cause: RUNNERS have no value-option table. Fix: give uv/poetry their value-taking options (or treat any post-runner token beginning with '-' that is unknown as possibly value-taking).

candidates.title: Empty ENVH_SESSION assignment makes a session-LESS run look in-session: `ENVH_SESSION= envh run ...` returns NO ASK
repro_cmds: echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "ENVH_SESSION= envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "export ENVH_SESSION=; envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
candidates.observed_output: All print nothing (NO ASK). Control `envh run --reason r -- echo hi` -> ASK. Client semantics proven: `ENVH_SESSION= python -c 'import os;print(repr(None or os.environ.get("ENVH_SESSION")), bool(None or os.environ.get("ENVH_SESSION")))'` prints "'' False".
candidates.why_novel: The hook decides 'in session' with `word.startswith(SESSION_ASSIGNMENT)` where SESSION_ASSIGNMENT == 'ENVH_SESSION='. An EMPTY assignment ('ENVH_SESSION=') satisfies startswith(), so in_session becomes True and passphrase_reason() returns None. But an empty value is NOT a session. Not acknowledged anywhere; the README treats ENVH_SESSION as a bearer token, never says an empty one is ignored.
candidates.notes: Really starts a request: bash `ENVH_SESSION= envh run ...` sets ENVH_SESSION to the empty string in envh's environment. client/commands.py cmd_run: `session_id = args.session or os.environ.get('ENVH_SESSION')` = `None or ''` = '' and sends op=run session=''. server/control.py op_run line 203-204 `session_id = message.get('session'); if session_id:` -> '' is falsy -> takes the session-LESS path (request_run, line 209-211) -> console passphrase prompt. Cleanest bypass: a plain one-liner, no external tools. Fix: treat an empty ENVH_SESSION value as no session (match the client/broker's own truthiness).

candidates.title: `env --split-string=`/`env -S` runs a nested command the hook never parses: `env --split-string="envh run ..."` returns NO ASK
candidates.observed_output: Both print nothing (NO ASK). GNU env behaviour proven: `env --split-string="printf arg0=%s;arg1=%s\n one two"` prints `arg0=one;arg1=two`, i.e. env splits the string into argv and execs it (coreutils 9.4).
candidates.why_novel: `env` is documented as a handled wrapper, and the hook knows env's value-options {-u,--unset,-C,--chdir}. But GNU env's -S/--split-string option both takes a value AND re-parses that value into a whole command line (like `bash -c`). The hook neither lists -S/--split-string as value-taking NOR recurses into its string as a nested script. command_words() sees the single token '--split-string=envh run ...' (or '-Senvh ...') as an unknown flag, index += 1, and returns [] -> no envh detected -> no ask. Not among the acknowledged bypasses; it is a command-runner the hook ignores entirely.
candidates.notes: Really starts a request: `env --split-string='envh run --reason r -- echo hi'` execs `envh run ...` (session-less -> prompt); `env -S'envh session start ...'` execs the session start (always prompts). GNU coreutils >= 8.30 (common on modern Linux). Fix: parse -S/--split-string's value as a nested script, exactly like bash -c/eval.

candidates.title: Nesting past MAX_NESTING=3 (chained eval / bash -c): `eval eval eval eval envh run ...` returns NO ASK
repro_cmds: echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "eval eval eval eval envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py

echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "bash -c 'eval eval eval envh session start weekly --minutes 5 --reason r'"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
candidates.observed_output: Both print nothing (NO ASK). Controls: `eval eval eval envh run --reason r -- echo hi` (3 levels) -> ASK. bash proven to collapse the chain: `eval eval eval eval echo X` runs the final echo.
candidates.why_novel: The docstring states the hook reads inside `bash -c` or `eval`. It recurses into nested scripts only while nesting < MAX_NESTING (=3), i.e. at levels 0,1,2, stopping at level 3; a 4th nested eval/bash -c is never parsed, so the envh inside it is missed. The depth cap is not an acknowledged bypass (the README lists only script file / interpreter one-liner / pipe / variable-built).
candidates.notes: Really starts a request: bash collapses `eval eval eval eval envh run ...` to `envh run ...` (session-less -> prompt); `bash -c 'eval eval eval envh session start ...'` is bash-c(level0->1) + 3 evals = level 4, and runs the session start (always prompts). Chained eval needs no exotic quoting. Fix: raise/remove the cap, or (safer) fall back to the PASSPHRASE_FORM regex when the cap is hit, as is already done for unclosed quotes.

candidates.title: `env -i` / `env -u ENVH_SESSION` strips the session the hook still counts: `ENVH_SESSION=x env -i envh run ...` returns NO ASK
repro_cmds: echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "ENVH_SESSION=deadbeef env -i envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py

echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "ENVH_SESSION=deadbeef env -u ENVH_SESSION envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py

echo '{"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "export ENVH_SESSION=abc && env -i envh run --reason r -- echo hi"}}' | /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
candidates.observed_output: All print nothing (NO ASK). Proven that env strips it before envh runs: `ENVH_SESSION=deadbeef env -i  python -c 'print(os.environ.get("ENVH_SESSION"))'` -> None; `env -u ENVH_SESSION ...` -> None. Control: `env -u ENVH_SESSION envh run ...` with NO prior assignment -> ASK (correct), so the bypass specifically needs the var present-then-stripped.
candidates.why_novel: The hook records in_session=True from an inline `ENVH_SESSION=<nonempty>` prefix (or a prior `export ENVH_SESSION=<nonempty>`) and keeps it for the following envh command. It does not model `env -i` (clear all env) or `env -u ENVH_SESSION` (unset that var) removing the session before envh runs. ENVH_SESSION detection error, not acknowledged.
candidates.notes: Really starts a request: `env -i`/`env -u ENVH_SESSION` means envh's process has no ENVH_SESSION, so cmd_run sends session=None -> session-less run -> prompt. Precondition: the session value must be set then stripped within the same command string (inline assignment or prior export), which is why a bare `env -u ENVH_SESSION envh run` correctly ASKS. Most contrived of the five, but valid. Fix: when a tracked ENVH_SESSION assignment is followed by `env -i`, or `env -u ENVH_SESSION`/`--unset ENVH_SESSION`, drop the in_session state.

negative_results: uv run --with=rich envh run ... (the equals/self-contained form) correctly ASKS; only the space-separated value form (w1-hook-1) bypasses.
uv run envh run ... (no uv options) correctly ASKS.
eval eval eval envh run ... (exactly 3 levels, within MAX_NESTING) correctly ASKS.
env -u ENVH_SESSION envh run ... with NO prior ENVH_SESSION assignment correctly ASKS (in_session stays False).
env -C /dir envh run ... and env FOO=bar envh run ... correctly ASK (known env value-options / assignments handled).
timeout 5 envh run, timeout -s TERM 5 envh run, nice -n 5 envh ..., nohup/setsid/exec/stdbuf/xargs wrappers all correctly ASK for a session-less run.
`command -v envh` returns no-ask (correct: it is only a lookup); `command -v envh && envh session start ...` correctly ASKS on the second command.

envh --socket /x run ... strips both --socket and the following word, but real envh (--socket needs a Path value, subcommand required after) would error rather than start a request, so there is no false negative there.
envh run --reason x -- mytool --session foo correctly ASKS: the trailing --session belongs to the run target, not to envh, and run_options only reads options before the first non-dash/`--`.

F11: yaml.safe_load is used in core/config.py (no yaml.load/Loader= anywhere); no eval/exec/os.system/pickle/marshal in src (only the acknowledged curl|sudo sh uv installer uses shell=True); src/envh/__init__.py is just __version__; pyproject.toml uses stock hatchling with no custom build hooks; nothing runs at import. No non-root import-time code-execution or unsafe-deserialization vector found.
out_of_scope_observations: F11: The wizard reruns its OWN root half straight from the agent-editable clone: `sudo /usr/bin/python3 <clone>/scripts/setup_wizard.py --install-as-root`. An agent that edits setup_wizard.py gets arbitrary code as root the moment the human runs the install step and types the sudo password. This is effectively acknowledged/inherent: the docstring says 'envh never runs from this folder, because agents can edit it', README says run the wizard in a terminal of its own, and the broker source (src/envh) is copied to root-only /opt/envh precisely because the clone is agent-writable. Loading platform.py by path from the staged copy (system_problems) defends only the preflight CHECKS, not the wizard script itself. Trusting the installer you run as root is inherent -> KNOWN, not claimed.

F11: uv.lock and src in the clone are agent-editable; `uv sync --frozen --no-editable` as root installs whatever the clone/lock specifies into /opt/envh, later run by envhsvc. Acknowledged (README: 'asks again if the clone has uncommitted changes, since root installs those too'; 'agents can edit the clone'). KNOWN.

F11: uv_for_root() (root half) resolves uv with shutil.which('uv') under the root process PATH and WITHOUT the root-ownership check that the user half's root_owned_uv() applies. On a sudoers configuration that does NOT set `secure_path` (not the default on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora), root's PATH can include a user-writable directory ahead of /usr/local/bin, so a user-planted `uv` could run as root even when a root-owned uv exists. Conditional on sudo config and not reproducible as a non-root user in this arena (cannot edit sudoers), so noted, not claimed.

F11 (acknowledged, non-root but known): `~/.local/bin/uv` being run as root (README: 'a uv in your home folder could be swapped by anything running as you'); `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sudo env ... sh` (README: 'runs astral.sh's installer as root'); desktop launcher shadowed by ~/.local/share/applications (README 'What envh does not do').

F11 (root-only, out of scope per CHARTER §3): /opt/envh, /usr/local/sbin/envh-console, /usr/share/applications/envh.desktop, /usr/local/bin/envh, and /var/lib/envh are all root- or envhsvc-owned; a normal user cannot write them.
